name: BitallxPayOut pays the amounts array without bounding it by the deposit
summary: BitallxSC.BitallxPayOut(token, wallet[], amount[], totalSendAmount) checks the caller's allowance and balance against totalSendAmount and pulls only that much, then transfers every amount[i] from the contract's own balance without checking that their sum equals totalSendAmount. The attacker's contract called it in its constructor with totalSendAmount 0 and one amount equal to the contract's whole balance, taking the 2,029.47 USDT held for reward claims; a copycat took 1,500 USDT the operator topped up a day later.
notes: Reset: deployment; the contract has no proxy and BitallxPayOut reads no stored configuration. The only earlier BitallxPayOut call (0xe376ed0f, block 49644066) paid out exactly the 4.3 USDT its caller deposited; all other earlier outflows are the publisher's claimReward payouts. The deployer later deployed a fixed BitallxSC (0xacc880be) whose payout sums the amounts and is owner-only.

Campaign: 0x5dc69e59 (from 0xd4f04374 through a generic executor 0x5100357b) took the 1,500 USDT that 0xafd99f65 deposited two blocks earlier; 0x2acd9130 took 10 GPT-4, an airdropped spam token with no market that the taker never sold, valued at 0 (rule 12). 0x59378096 called it with nothing left to take, and 0xfee5703b recovered 0.11 USDT its own sender had sent to the contract in 0xf8ba6103, so neither depleted a victim.
